## Verdict: REJECT (one checklist FAIL at the Important threshold: a false claim in docs/external/rule-sets.md)
The PR is not ready to merge, because the new restart advice in `docs/external/rule-sets.md` says a renamed or dropped table fails with the database's own error, but SQL Lens blocks that query first with its own redacted refusal.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major
- VC-18: FAIL (important) — Until restart, a query reaching a renamed or dropped name fails with the database's own error [docs/external/rule-sets.md] [behavior-inert prose cap] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: first-conjunct=held (the sentence at docs/external/rule-sets.md:197 describes runtime behavior; making it true changes no output, branch or covered set of relations.py or RefusalRedactingRunner) limb-one=held (no tool or agent reads the published doc page as instructions) limb-two=not-held (docs/external/ is a published operator doc page) -->

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Doc docs/external/rule-sets.md:197 says a query reaching a renamed or dropped name fails with the database's own error, naming table and column. That holds for a dropped or renamed column: RefusalRedactingRunner.run_sql (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:996-1016) catches only RuleSetRefusal, UnsafeSqlError and RlsError, so a pymysql error passes through. It does not hold for a dropped or renamed table. RuleSetGuardRunner always calls the inner runner with require_base_tables=True (rule_sets.py:894-896). The MySQL runner then calls verify_base_tables (agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:156-157) BEFORE executing the SQL. _verify_relations (safety/relations.py:171-188) looks the table up in information_schema.TABLES. For a missing table kind is None, so it raises RlsError 'row-level security could not verify a base table; query blocked'. RefusalRedactingRunner converts this to REDACTED_RELATION, 'refusing to execute query: the query's relations could not be verified' (rule_sets.py:953-954, 1005-1016). The query never reaches the database, so the client sees a redacted refusal rather than the database's own error. Counterexample: rule-set table renamed or dropped while the server runs. The claim as worded (renamed or dropped name, absolute) is therefore wrong for tables, and the 'error text can name the table' part is also false there. Only column drift matches.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)
<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` line 281: `InheritRule.parent_rule` is typed as the full `RowRule` union, so the column-local limit is enforced only by `RuleSet._check_row_rules`. Callers of `_rule_nodes` must walk `parent_rule` by hand, as `_check_row_rules` and `_catalog_reads` do today. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 433-436: the "allowed kinds" error message reads kind names through `model_fields["kind"].annotation.__args__[0]`. It would raise while reporting a validation error if a `kind` annotation stopped being a one-argument `Literal`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `tests/unit/test_row_rule_additions.py` lines 1016-1021: `test_a_file_using_only_the_six_shapes_compiles_as_before` compares the new compiler with itself, not with the SQL the base branch produced, so it cannot detect a change in how the six existing shapes compile. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `tests/unit/test_row_rule_additions.py` lines 989-1013: the new tests check generated SQL with `re.findall` and `str.startswith` instead of parsing it with sqlglot. This is test code, so runtime behavior is not affected, but a sqlglot formatting change can break these checks. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (2)
<details><summary>2 items</summary>

- VC-6: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — exp.Is(column, exp.Null()) generates as `x IS NULL` and exp.Not(exp.Paren(exp.Is(...))) generates as `NOT (x IS NULL)` in the mysql dialect and re-parses to the same tree, so prove_compiled_rule accepts it [src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:635]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The compile side matches the claim: src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:634-643 builds exp.Is(column, exp.Null()) for IsNullRule and exp.Not(exp.Paren(exp.Is(...))) for IsNotNullRule. prove_compiled_rule (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:445-450) generates the body, re-parses it, and compares _shape trees. requirements.txt:103 pins sqlglot==30.31.0. The item has no dependency_sources, the views contain no sqlglot source, and a Glob for sqlglot/generator.py under the review directory found nothing. I therefore could not read the MySQL generator or parser, and I did not run any code. tests/unit/test_row_rule_additions.py:225 expects 'NOT (`a0`.`deleted_at` IS NULL)', which is consistent with the claim but is not the library's behaviour. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.31.0 generator and parser source, or a run of the unit tests.

  </details>

- VC-14: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — MySQL error codes asserted: EXP(1000) overflow raises 1690 and an unknown column raises 1054, and pymysql exposes them as error.args[0] [tests/connectors/test_row_rule_additions_mysql.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The test asserts error.args[0] == 1690 for _RAISE (IF(id = N, EXP(1000), 0) > 0, test_row_rule_additions_mysql.py:174,193) and == 1054 for a renamed column (line 329); _error catches pymysql.err.MySQLError (lines 132-135). My recollection is that MySQL ER_DATA_OUT_OF_RANGE is 1690 and ER_BAD_FIELD_ERROR is 1054, and that pymysql raises MySQLError(errno, msg), so args[0] is the errno. The item has no dependency_sources, and the views do not contain pymysql source or the MySQL error reference, so I could not read either to confirm. I did not run the tests against a live MySQL.

  </details>

</details>
